sentences.text: Sinopterus is an extinct genus of pterodactyloid pterosaurs from the Early Cretaceous found in the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning, China.
The animal possessed a large, toothless, bird-like beak and a long bony crest extending from the front of the skull to a point over the rear.
It is characterized by a proportionally long skull equipped with a toothless beak resembling that of birds, and it possessed a long bony crest directed backward and ending in a point.
Adult Sinopterus could reach a maximum wingspan of 1.9 meters and weigh 2.87 kilograms.
Scientists have identified at least one very small juvenile or hatchling specimen, and studies suggest that juvenile Sinopterus could fly using powered flight rather than just gliding.
Late juvenile Sinopterus reached sexual maturity at about 79% of adult size before completing skeletal growth.
The genus Sinopterus was first described by Wang and Zhou in 2003.
The type species Sinopterus dongi is known from a single specimen described in 2003, which is based on the holotype IVPP V13363, an articulated and nearly complete skeleton.
This holotype had a skull 17 centimeters long and a wingspan of 1.2 meters.
A second specimen, BPV-077, was described in 2003 as a separate species, Sinopterus gui, named by Li, Lü, and Zhang.
In 2023, Pêgas and colleagues reviewed the taxonomy of tapejarids and synonymized several Sinopterus species with S. dongi.
Evidence from gut contents suggests that Sinopterus was a herbivore.

In 2025, researchers reported finding stomach contents within the abdominal cavity of a Sinopterus specimen, including gastroliths and phytoliths, marking the first evidence of these items co-occurring in a pterosaur.
Bite force estimations and skull similarities suggest Sinopterus had a herbivorous diet of fruits, seeds, and resistant plant matter.
The scarcity of adult fossils compared to juveniles suggests Sinopterus may have been migratory, with adults living in different habitats than younger individuals.
The parent group of Sinopterus is the family Tapejaridae, and the genus is classified within the class Reptilia.
A 2014 analysis placed Sinopterus species within the clade Tapejaromorpha.
Fossils of Sinopterus date to the Early Cretaceous period, and Sinopterus lived during the Aptian age of the Early Cretaceous in Chaoyang, Liaoning, China.
Sinopterus lived during the Aptian stage, from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
Researchers debate whether multiple Sinopterus species exist, suggesting many differences are actually growth variations within a single species.

S. gui differs from S. dongi mainly by its smaller size and the presence of a notarium, though this distinction is controversial, and many subsequent studies have found that S. gui simply represents a younger specimen of S. dongi.
